cases.exposure_context_quote: The patient himself, upon recovery, recalled possibly ingesting contaminated food in the days preceding symptom onset, though the exact source was unclear.
cases.agent_quote: The test returned a high serum concentration of Brodifacoum at 77.86 ng/mL.
cases.circumstance: unclear exposure history; family could not provide a definitive history of rodenticide exposure; no anticoagulant medication use

symptoms.quote: A 69-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with a 9-day history of oral bleeding and an 8-day history of pain in the lower back, abdomen, and chest.

symptoms.finding: pain in lower back, abdomen, and chest (8-day history)
symptoms.quote: A 69-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with a 9-day history of oral bleeding and an 8-day history of pain in the lower back, abdomen, and chest.

symptoms.finding: pain in right calf and both upper limbs
symptoms.quote: Three days before admission, he developed pain in his right calf and both upper limbs.

symptoms.finding: large ecchymosis on right upper limb
symptoms.quote: Physical examination on the day of admission revealed a blood pressure of 146/96 mmHg, active oral bleeding, and a large ecchymosis on the right upper limb.

symptoms.finding: aortic dissection from distal abdominal aorta to bilateral iliac arteries with intramural hematoma
symptoms.quote: Aortic computed tomography angiography (CTA) confirmed an extensive aortic dissection involving the distal abdominal aorta down to the bilateral iliac arteries (Figures 1, 2).

cases.time_to_care: UNVERIFIED (admitted 9 days after symptom onset of oral bleeding; time from exposure to care not stated)

labs.name: prothrombin time (PT)
labs.quote: both prothrombin time (PT) and the international normalized ratio (INR) were unmeasurably high

labs.name: INR
labs.quote: both prothrombin time (PT) and the international normalized ratio (INR) were unmeasurably high

labs.name: APTT
labs.quote: the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) was markedly prolonged to 160.1 s

labs.name: hemoglobin
labs.quote: Persistent bleeding led to moderate-to-severe anemia, with hemoglobin decreasing from 102 g/L to 88 g/L

labs.name: serum brodifacoum (GC/MS)
labs.quote: The test returned a high serum concentration of Brodifacoum at 77.86 ng/mL.

labs.name: alanine aminotransferase
labs.quote: normal liver function (alanine aminotransferase 9.20 U/L and aspartate aminotransferase 14.90 U/L)

labs.name: aspartate aminotransferase
labs.quote: normal liver function (alanine aminotransferase 9.20 U/L and aspartate aminotransferase 14.90 U/L)

treatment.name: fresh frozen plasma (initial 300 mL bolus, then 400 mL daily for 5 days)
treatment.quote: The patient received an initial bolus transfusion of 300 mL of FFP upon admission, followed by daily transfusions of 400 mL for the next five consecutive days

treatment.name: high-dose intravenous vitamin K1 (10 mg every 12 h, tapered to 10 mg once daily)
treatment.quote: high-dose intravenous vitamin K1 was administered at 10 mg every 12 h

treatment.name: oral metoprolol sustained-release 47.5 mg once daily
treatment.quote: This was achieved with oral metoprolol sustained-release (47.5 mg once daily) to reduce heart rate and contractility

treatment.name: oral felodipine sustained-release 5 mg once daily
treatment.quote: and oral felodipine sustained-release (5 mg once daily) for vasodilation

cases.outcome: stabilized; coagulation parameters normalized over two weeks; discharged with long-term outpatient follow-up; dissection stable with hematoma resolution at 1-month CTA
cases.outcome_quote: The patient's condition was stabilized through aggressive management, including infusion of fresh frozen plasma (FFP), high-dose intravenous vitamin K, and strict blood pressure control. His coagulation parameters gradually normalized over two weeks.
cases.sequelae: persistent but stable aortic dissection (dissection flap and intramural hematoma remained stable, with hematoma resolution at 1-month follow-up CTA)
cases.notes: Blood pressure on admission 146/96 mmHg; BP targets 100–120 mmHg systolic, HR 60–80 bpm. Final diagnoses: extensive aortic dissection and severe acquired coagulopathy due to superwarfarin (brodifacoum) poisoning.
